newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX index stays ahead, off earlier highs.
newsitem.headline: German DAX index stays ahead, off earlier highs.

text.p: German shares continued their dollar-driven rally in afternoon IBIS trade on Wednesday and while dealers still forecast a correction, they said they will make the most of the bull-run for as long as it lasts.
Shares came off earlier highs, however, as Wall Street opened lower, to stand at 3,012.90 points, up 12.24.

"It's the strong dollar that is underpinning everything today and no-one can afford to be out of the market," said one trader. "People are waiting for the plug to come out of the market. They are letting it go up now, but don't trust it in the long term."
The Dow Jones Industrial index was down over one percent at 6,811.93 points early on, which combined with a weakening of the dollar to 1.6361/64 marks to scupper earlier gains.
At one point the IBIS DAX earlier hit 3,043.06 points while the dollar traded well above 1.64 marks.
While weak U.S. housing data before the opening bell had been expected to boost Wall Street, a sharply lower opening for giant IBM put U.S. stocks under pressure earlier on.
Even in its slightly weaker position in the afternoon, the relative strength of the dollar did much to boost German exporting stocks.
Deutsche Bank, the heaviest-traded stock, remained in favour as part of a sector rotation which saw the bank gain 1.21 marks to 83.48 marks, albeit off earlier highs at 84.37.

Other star performers included car stocks, especially Daimler-Benz AG and Volkswagen AG. Daimler rose 1.20 marks to 114.50 marks in afternoon IBIS trade, while Volkswagen advanced 25 marks to 767 marks.
"Daimler, Volkswagen are all having a great day and they are all dollar-driven. People are looking now to Siemens to outperform, because it's been an underperformer for so long," said the trader.
There was big turnover in Siemens AG shares, the second most-sought-after German stock in afternoon electronic trade, which was up 18 pfennigs at 78.55 marks.
Dollar strength also lifted German chemical stocks -- BASF AG was up 1.36 marks at 59.75 marks, Bayer AG was up 1.07 marks at 62.35 marks and Hoechst AG was up 95 pfennigs at 69.90 marks.
